newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity down on mild weather, hydro.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity down on mild weather, hydro.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed lower amid mild weather conditions and plentiful hydroelectric generation in the western U.S., trade sources said Monday.
"The only thing that may throw a fly in the ointment is you have to be cautious about betting on mild weather at COB (California-Oregon border) for the next month or so," said one trader.
If rivers in the Pacific Northwest start to freeze, utilities will move to combustion turbines for power generation, leading to prices of $25.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) or more, the trader explained.
Market sources also cited weaker natural gas prices and lackluster holiday trading as contributing to Monday's drop in power futures.
"Natural gas was down 30 cents. That didn't provide strength at Palo," said one trader.

February 1997 COB futures lost $1.04 to close at $14.20 per MWh, while the March contract was down 70 cents at $13.00. February Palo Verde was down by $1.16 at $15.28, while March fell 80 cents to $14.70. Other PV contracts finished narrowly mixed.
